headline: High: shared writable project/workspace paths and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Devin and gpt-engineer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while gpt-engineer writes files in a user project directory and reads filesystem content. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from shared files or integrations. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or synced workspace
IF either agent parses the other's generated files as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP inputs for Devin during the run
Require a human review step before one agent consumes the other's files
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion write scopes. gpt-engineer reads and writes a project directory and sends prompts to a configured model. If sensitive material lands in the shared workspace, both agents can expose it through their outbound APIs; the exact data path is docs-based, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF sensitive source code, tickets, or chat content is placed in the shared project directory
IF either agent forwards that content to external APIs or writes it into synced integrations
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use separate credentials for each agent
Restrict outbound integrations to a test workspace
Redact sensitive files before either agent runs
Rotate any tokens exposed in shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Devin can modify git state while gpt-engineer writes into the project directory with no default isolation. In a shared repo, concurrent edits can clobber branches, generated code, or workspace state. Because Devin also has broader integration reach, the conflict blast radius is larger than a simple local overwrite.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or project directory
IF they run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable one agent's git writes during the other's run
Use disposable worktrees for each agent
Review and merge changes manually

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run generated code. If Devin consumes gpt-engineer's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or executed commands without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer reading is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Devin treats gpt-engineer's generated files as trusted input
IF generated code or instructions are executed without an independent review step
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before execution
Require tests to pass before either agent acts on the other's output
Limit Devin to drafting only, not execution
Have gpt-engineer emit patches instead of runnable commands
Compare outputs against a known-good spec

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly touches team chat, issue trackers, and docs and requests Slack/Jira/Notion write scopes, while gpt-engineer is scoped to a project directory and model API calls. If regulated or sensitive content is present, the pair can move it into third-party services with different retention and residency terms. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the project directory or linked tickets
IF Slack, Jira, or Notion are used for that data without matching retention and residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Slack/Jira/Notion
Use a non-regulated sandbox project
Apply retention settings before the run
Restrict the agents to synthetic data
Document the data flow for compliance review
